newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GOVERNMENT APPROVES PLAN TO RAISE ENERGY VAT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GOVERNMENT APPROVES PLAN TO RAISE ENERGY VAT.

text.p: The Czech government approved a plan on Wednesday to raise the value added tax on electricity and natural gas to 22 percent from five percent, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news conference.
The hike in the energy VAT, which must still be approved by parliament as do all changes in the tax code, would begin on January 1, 1998, Klaus said.
"The government expressed its agreement with the movement of fuels and energies (VAT) from five percent to 22 percent, from January (next year)," Klaus said.

He said the government had a "global" agreement in priniciple on raising regulated housing rents, but that the details were still to be worked out. Klaus said he was the cabinet meeting would continue on this subject.

Party leaders of the ruling three-party coalition agreed late last month to raise state-controlled rents by an average of about 50 percent nationwide from July 1, but they have been discussing social compensation to offset the rise for low income households. The decision requires formal cabinet approval.
The cabinet had yet to discuss its planned agenda items on changes in corporate and personal income taxes and excise taxes, scheduled for Wednesday.

Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy has been quoted in local media as saying that he would demand an across the board decrease in the top VAT rate next year in return for his support for the energy VAT increase this year.
The plan to hike VAT on energy is a part of a price deregulation plan aimed at bringing household prices in line with prices for industry, which are currently notably higher.
Private TV Nova reported on Tuesday that the Finance Ministry would propose to cut corporate tax next year to 35 percent from 39 percent and to widen income brackets for personal income tax.
